extracted.intended_audience: researchers and applicants seeking Multiple Sclerosis Research Program (MSRP) / CDMRP funding; stakeholders (service members, veterans, consumers)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Multiple Sclerosis Research Program's vision, mission, research priorities, target beneficiaries, and review/administrative expectations for applicants and stakeholders. Useful for investigators preparing applications to align proposals with program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent, cure, reverse, or slow the progression, and lessen the personal and societal impact of multiple sclerosis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching long-term goal proposals should support; alignment with preventing, curing, reversing, slowing progression, or lessening MS impact is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: To support pioneering concepts and high-impact research relevant to the prevention, etiology, pathogenesis, assessment, treatment, and ultimate cure of multiple sclerosis for the benefit of Service Members and their Families, Veterans, and the American public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should emphasize pioneering (novel) concepts and potential for high impact across the listed research domains; beneficiary populations (Service Members, Families, Veterans, public) are explicitly named priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Focus Areas (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research relevant to the prevention, etiology, pathogenesis, assessment, treatment, and ultimate cure of multiple sclerosis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should clearly map their aims to one or more of these focus areas; scope includes basic, translational, clinical, and assessment-related work that advances understanding or management of MS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on Innovative and Impactful Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Since its inception in fiscal year 2009, the Multiple Sclerosis Research Program (MSRP) has supported innovative and impactful research that addresses fundamental issues and gaps in MS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program prioritizes projects that are novel/pioneering and that address fundamental gaps; novelty and potential for substantial impact are important evaluation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Beneficiary Populations
rubrics_metrics.description: For the benefit of Service Members and their Families, Veterans, and the American public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While broadly applicable MS research may be supported, proposals that explicitly address needs or benefits for Service Members, Veterans, and their families are especially aligned with program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Tiered Review and Programmatic Oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Two Tiered Review Process (programmatic panels and peer review participants are part of the program's review structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be evaluated through CDMRP's two-tiered review (including programmatic panels and peer review). Applicants should be aware that both scientific/technical review and programmatic relevance influence funding decisions; consult Programmatic Panels and Peer Review Participants pages for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Involvement in Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer Involvement / Program Consumer Reviewer Requirements (consumer reviewers participate in CDMRP processes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer (lay) reviewers contribute to evaluation; applicants should consider the clarity and translational/real-world relevance of proposals for non-technical reviewers and consult consumer reviewer guidance where provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Research Duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding Research Duplication (applicants are directed to resources on avoiding duplication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate awareness of existing funded work and justify novelty/need to avoid redundant research; applicants should use the program's duplication-avoidance resources and the searchable awards database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Program Resources and Strategic Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Summary Sheet and Strategic Plan are available (clickable resources referenced on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the MSRP Program Summary Sheet and Strategic Plan to align aims with program priorities and strategic objectives; these documents provide more detailed priority areas and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of Funding History and Prior Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional Appropriations, Funding Summary, and list of awards (e.g., 239 Awards in FY09-24) are provided on the program page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can review prior funded projects and funding levels to understand program emphasis and competitiveness; use the 'Search Awards' and 'FY24 MSRP Recommended for Funding List' links to inform proposal framing and innovation claims.
